newsitem.title: INDIA: India Essel shares up on buy-back news.
newsitem.headline: India Essel shares up on buy-back news.

text.p: Shares of India's Essel Packaging, a leading manufacturer of laminated tubes, rose 9.75 rupees or six percent, to 169.50 at the Bombay bourse on Friday on news that the firm plans a share buy-back at a premium, traders said.

The share buy-back of about 10-20 percent of the company's 150 million rupee equity capital is likely to be done at about 225 rupees per share, the Economic Times newspaper on Friday quoted Subhash Chandra, chairman of Essel Packaging, as saying.
The company will buy back shares from the market after the government grants permission to Indian companies, the report said. Essel officials were not immediately available for comment.
Sales of Essel Packaging rose 27 percent to 325.1 million rupees in the first quarter ending June 30, 1997 against the year-ago period, the paper said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his budget proposals for the 1997/98 (April-March) said that buy-backs of shares would be allowed under a new company law for which a legislative bill would be introduced in parliament.
